extracted.intended_audience: general readers and policymakers interested in post‑war international trade and employment policy
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and exposition of proposed principles, institutional arrangements, and procedural steps for expanding world trade and employment after World War II (including creation of an International Trade Organization and detailed rules on tariffs, quotas, subsidies, cartels, and settlement of sterling balances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on emergency restrictions (non-discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions may be permitted to assist a country whose economy has been disrupted by war only where there is special necessity and where measures do not involve a substantial departure from the general rule of non-discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions (e.g., to assist war-disrupted economies) should be narrowly tailored and must not substantially depart from non-discrimination principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity with IMF authority for exchange restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A government is authorized to impose exchange or quantitative restrictions in conformity with Article ___ of the articles of agreement of the International Monetary Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange restrictions must be justified under IMF rules and become effective as soon as practicable (text specified a deadline: not later than Dec. 31, 1946).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement categories for accumulated sterling balances
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterling balances accumulated prior to settlement should be divided into three categories: (A) balances to be released at once and convertible for current transactions; (B) balances to be converted by installments over specified years; (C) balances to be adjusted as a contribution to settlement of war and post‑war indebtedness and in recognition of benefits to the countries concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlements with sterling‑area countries are to be negotiated on this tripartite basis; the UK government will endeavor to secure early completion of these arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds and credit for multilateral trade must be non-discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Line of credit established to promote multilateral trade should be freely available for current transactions in any currency area without discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial support aimed at promoting multilateral trade must not favor particular currency areas or countries; availability should be equal on economic grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for negotiation clarity (e.g., 'current transactions', 'sterling area')
rubrics_metrics.description: Key terms used in proposals are to be defined (for example, 'current transactions' as in IMF Article XIX(1); 'sterling area' enumerated by territorial orders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise legal/technical definitions should be included so negotiators have a common understanding of terms used in agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to seek reconsideration of agreement provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Either government shall be entitled to approach the other for reconsideration of any provisions of the agreement if prevailing conditions of international exchange justify such reconsideration, with a view to agreeing upon modifications for presentation to their Legislatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements should include formal mechanisms for review and modification when exchange conditions materially change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive reduction of government-imposed trade restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad and detailed agreement among many nations should deal at one time with many different sorts of governmental restrictions upon trade, reducing all of them at once on a balanced and equitable basis and stating rules and principles within which the restrictions permitted to remain should be administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiations should be extensive and simultaneous across many barrier types (tariffs, quotas, preferences, administrative burdens) to avoid piecemeal or discriminatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, detailed negotiations prior to conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective preparation for the Conference must include detailed negotiations on trade barriers to commence as soon as possible and to continue until every friendly country has participated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiations should start before the general Conference convenes and continue afterward; not all countries must be at the table at once but work should progress quickly and inclusively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and narrowly define quotas and embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotas and embargoes should be limited to carefully defined goods and applied only where the need is real and serious, affecting many people and not curable by other measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls of this sort should not be applied unless truly necessary; definitions and scope must be precise to avoid abuse and disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary nature and international administration of special measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Special measures (e.g., temporary commodity agreements, subsidies used for adjustment, semi‑permanent controls during transition) should be strictly temporary, limited in duration, and administered with the assistance of an international staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional arrangements must include time limits and international oversight to prevent permanent distortions or protectionism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair treatment by government trade agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies of governments conducting foreign trade should give fair treatment to the commerce of friendly states, make purchases and sales on economic grounds, and avoid using a monopoly of imports to afford excessive protection to domestic producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public procurement and state trading should be administered on economic, non‑discriminatory bases; avoid import monopolies being used as disguised protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full publicity about international schemes and participation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be full publicity about each scheme so the world may be sure it is managed in the general interest; affected countries should be entitled to participate and have an equal voice in administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and inclusive governance are essential; arrangements should publicly disclose terms and allow participation by concerned states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement against private combines and cartels
rubrics_metrics.description: Private agreements that divide markets (combines/cartels) should be brought under supervision; enforcement against private violators necessarily rests with member governments applying their laws and procedures, with the Organization able to receive complaints, examine facts and advise remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International organization should have a complaints/examination function and recommend remedies, but actual enforcement will ordinarily require action by national authorities under their laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid governmental or intergovernmental measures that export unemployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each country will seek to maintain full and regular production on its own account and not do so by using measures which would damage other countries or prevent the expansion of world trade (i.e., do not export unemployment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National stabilization/anti‑depression policies should be coordinated and consulted internationally to avoid beggar‑thy‑neighbor outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of information and consultation on anti-depression programs
rubrics_metrics.description: All countries will cooperate in exchanging information and participate in consultations with respect to anti‑depression policies, and the Organization should examine measures adopted that have effects abroad and advise on fair rules of mutual tolerance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular consultation and information exchange are required so national policies reinforce rather than cancel each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization of new trade agency with existing international agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: An International Trade Organization should be established and brought into relation with existing agencies (currency, investment, agriculture, labor, civil aviation) and harmonize policies with respect to international trade and employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should mirror other UN agencies and coordinate across related international functions for coherent policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to markets and raw materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose is to make real the principle of equal access to the markets and the raw materials of the world, so that varied national capacities can contribute to common welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade rules should aim at non‑discriminatory access to both markets and essential inputs to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit local taxes on imports to parity with like domestic products
rubrics_metrics.description: Local taxes on imported products would be limited to rates no higher than those levied on like products produced at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax parity prevents disguised protection via local taxation and promotes fair competition between domestic and imported goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidies and export subsidies treated cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidies (especially export subsidies) can be harmful and self‑defeating; when used for adjustment they should be strictly temporary and not designed to secure unfair advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules should aim to eliminate or tightly limit export subsidies and ensure any temporary aids have clear exit timetables and international oversight.
